evidence: The paper employs tree-based models (random forest and ISLE) but reports only predictive performance measures: "The logistic lasso, logistic elastic-net, and tree-based methods yielded AUCs comparable to those of the logistic regression with subject-matter knowledge." Variables are selected via cross-validated AUC optimization on a 75/25 train-test split, not by impurity importance ranking. The authors conclude: "Appropriate machine learning methods can substitute our knowledge of target conditions to construct CBAs efficiently," referring to overall model selection, not variable importance interpretation. Input features span 1,333 ICD-10 codes (89.6% appearing in <1% of samples) and 92 WHO-ATC codes, with continuous demographics (age, gender), creating mixed-type, high-cardinality, skewed feature sets.
